description: The graph illustrates the loss evolution over iterations for various models, including Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and SepLLM variants with different configurations (n=64, n=64, H, and n=64, H/T), as well as SepLLM (n=128). The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000, with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis denotes the loss, scaled linearly from 2.4 to 3.4. All models begin with a high loss value near 3.3 and exhibit a sharp initial decline within the first 20,000 iterations. After this initial phase, the loss curves for all models converge and stabilize, showing a gradual decrease towards a final loss value around 2.5. The SepLLM (n=128) model, represented by a dark blue solid line, consistently maintains the lowest loss across the entire iteration range, followed closely by the SepLLM (n=64, H/T) model (red line). The SepLLM (n=64) model (orange line) and SepLLM (n=64, H) model (green line) show very similar performance, with the SepLLM (n=64, H) slightly lower than the SepLLM (n=64). The StrmLLM (n=64) model (light blue line) shows a slightly higher loss compared to the SepLLM variants. The Vanilla model (purple line) exhibits the highest loss throughout the training process, indicating less effective convergence.
